_: Departures from design/spec/S2-S5-20260915T2224Z/index.css, the S2 slice. Each entry carries the body it declares, so a second, different change to the same rule cannot inherit this label.

_slice.why: S2's spec block is a whole page, so it carries about ninety card-internal rules that belong to S2b, which has no PR yet. DROPPED is enforced for this spec only once S2b is actually in the tree.

facts.means: the card sheet is APPLIED to the page. Not 'the file exists': src/app/redesign-card.css is committed inert on SDE-App's branch, imported by nothing, so the transcription could be reviewed before it could move a pixel. Presence would arm this gate with the card still the legacy block.

the markup the sheet styles is really rendering. The snapshot's own card is a stack of div.phase[data-phase], and the transcription keeps the attribute, so this is design-anchored rather than invented.

.card.claim.why: `will-change:height` for the panel animation, which the frozen preview does not need because its demo machine swaps panels without animating the box.

.mascot-riso.why: The owner's 19:40Z ruling says the mascot follows its column. The frozen snapshot does NOT carry the !important width/max-width/height that the ruling describes - grep finds none on that rule - so the ruling's intent is transcribed here and the discrepancy between the ruling's words and the snapshot is recorded in the PR body rather than silently resolved either way.
.mascot-riso.shipped: position:relative; display:block; flex:none; width:100%; max-width:calc(22*var(--u)); aspect-ratio:1; padding:0; border:0; background:transparent; appearance:none; cursor:pointer; user-select:none; touch-action:manipulation || width:100% !important; max-width:calc(22*var(--u)) !important; height:auto !important

.stage .card.claim.why: The card's own padding, which the design carries on .card-copy - a wrapper our current content does not sit inside. Every other parity probe measures a DESIGN element; this is CURRENT content inside a design container. S2b replaces this block with the real panels and takes this rule with it.

.tag.why: Our tag is a button or an anchor as well as a span, so it carries cursor and transition that a static pill in the preview has no need of.
.tag.shipped: font-family:inherit; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:calc(.5*var(--u)); height:calc(2.15*var(--u)); padding:0 calc(.9*var(--u)); border-radius:calc(.5*var(--u)); background:var(--tag-bg); color:var(--ink); font-size:calc(.84*var(--u)); font-weight:500; letter-spacing:0; border:calc(.06*var(--u)) solid var(--hair); white-space:nowrap; text-decoration:none; cursor:default || text-transform:none

.views > .view.hero.why: The spec has this as `.comp > .view.hero`. Our four views sit inside a <main class="views"> landmark rather than directly in .comp, so the child combinator matched nothing at all and computed padding-top 0. Same rule, our structure.

@media (max-width:56rem) | .mascot-riso.why: Same ruling, the narrow breakpoint: the cap that keeps the fox inside its column at phone widths, which the snapshot's own rule does not express.

@media (max-width:64rem) | .hero-grid.why: The 64rem block ships the gap and NOT grid-template-columns:1fr. That declaration was dead in the snapshot - a later section overrode it - and moving the block into this sheet brought it to life, collapsing the hero to one column from 897 to 1024px. Dropped deliberately; #566's third round is the record.

html.why: globals.css paints `html` with the OLD palette's --color-bg and nothing in the transcription names html's background, so the overscroll and rubber-band area behind the page kept the pre-redesign colour while the page itself was on --page. Only visible on a bounce, which is why nobody would find it by looking.
